hypothesis: If interface_compat blocks only changes that stop a previously valid value or record from being valid (a type swapped or narrowed, a field removed or renamed, a field made required, an enum value removed, a constraint tightened, a oneOf/anyOf alternative dropped) and makes widening changes advisory (type widened or made nullable, a required field made optional, an explicit type added that the existing enum already satisfies, a format added, oneOf/anyOf alternatives added, a draft-4 exclusive flag relaxed), then the share of held-out safe changes blocked will drop from 0.10 to 0.05 or less (no more than incumbent + 0.05). Breaking changes approved should stay near 0, because every breaking class seen in dev and in observed failures (type swap, field removed, field renamed, required added, enum value removed) is still blocked.
change_summary: Revised candidate/validators/interface_compat.mjs in place. (1) Type check: it now blocks only when a type that was allowed before is no longer allowed (integer counts as covered by number). A pure widening, such as adding a type or making a field nullable, is now advisory 'type_widened'. (2) Adding an explicit type to a field that had only enum/const is advisory when every existing value already has that type. Before, any newly stated type blocked. (3) Making a required field optional (required_removed) is now advisory instead of blocking. (4) A newly added format is advisory. Changing one format or unit value to another still blocks. (5) A draft-4 boolean exclusiveMinimum/Maximum blocks only when it goes from false or absent to true. Relaxing it is advisory. (6) oneOf/anyOf: adding alternatives is advisory. Dropping or changing an alternative, or adding a new oneOf/anyOf, still blocks. Removing the keyword is advisory. Any change to allOf, not or $ref still blocks. I updated the header comment to match. Result of `node check.mjs`: 60 cases, accuracy 1.0, 0 of 38 breaking changes approved, 0 of 22 safe changes blocked, no errors. Limitation: running anything other than `node check.mjs` was denied in this environment, so I could not run ad-hoc tests of the new widening branches. They are checked by reading the code only, not by execution.
procedure_step: For each field present before and after, block only if some value or record that was valid under contract_before is invalid under contract_after (a type lost, a field required, an enum value removed, a constraint tightened, an alternative dropped), or if the field was removed or renamed. Treat changes that only widen what is accepted as advisory.
known_failure_cases: If the held-out labels treat 'field made nullable' or 'required -> optional' as breaking (the consumer-read view), the check now approves them, and breaking changes approved rises above 0.
A pattern change that only loosens the pattern (e.g. a broader regex) is still blocked, because regex containment cannot be decided structurally. That is a false alarm if such a case appears.
Adding a format to a field that had none is now advisory. If a held-out case labels that as a breaking tightening, it will be missed.
A refactor that is semantically equivalent but changes allOf or $ref (e.g. moving an inline schema into $ref/$defs) is still blocked. That is a false alarm.
Adding additionalProperties: false to an object whose existing records never carried extra keys is still blocked.
A unit annotation added or dropped (x-unit undefined <-> value) is advisory. A unit that changes meaning through a renamed key, such as moving from 'unit' to 'x-unit', is not detected.
A rename where the new field's schema also differs is reported as field_removed rather than field_renamed. It is still blocked on the old path, so the outcome is right but the class name is not.
remaining_uncertainty: I don't know which safe class caused the 10% false-alarm rate. My leading guesses are type widening/nullable and required -> optional, and I relaxed several possible causes at once. Each relaxation trades some risk of approving breaking changes for fewer false alarms.
The dev set has no cases of type widening, required -> optional, format addition, oneOf/anyOf edits, or draft-4 exclusive flags, so none of the new branches is exercised by `node check.mjs`.
Ad-hoc execution beyond `node check.mjs` was denied, so the new code paths (covers/valueType, the composition handling) have not been run against hand-built inputs.

Whether 'made nullable' is breaking depends on the labeling convention: whether old records must stay valid, or whether consumers reading new data must not break. I chose the old-records-stay-valid view, which matches the dev labels for required_added and enum_value_removed.
